I loved the phone but could not get a signal when I was at home unless I went outside in the yard and I could NOT get the WiFi Calling feature to work so I returned it. Moto G7 with Alexa Does works with Metro, but you need to call them to connect.... Moto G7 with Alexa Does not work with Metro! Purchased on Amazon's Prime day and the phone did not connect with Metro's network. No matter what I tried and how many times and ways I tried to reset Moto G7 it was not working. I requested a replacement from Amazon and to my disappointment when it arrived it was identical to the first one. I called Motorola support line and their tech support informed me that this model is not compatible with Metro and I should switch to another carrier. Amazon describes G7 as "Moto G7 with Alexa Hands-Free - Unlocked - 64 GB - Ceramic Black (US Warranty) - Verizon, AT&T, T-Mobile, Sprint, Boost, Cricket, & Metro"... Buyer beware this device is not going to work on Metro. After some research it seems that the version with Alexa is the one with the issue.

Motorola shortchanges US customers. I've owned Moto phones since the original Razr, but I have a problem with being forced to pay a higher price for inferior selection or specs of the same model lines in the US compared to the rest of the world. In case you didn't know, that's Motorola's current US business strategy. Here are some examples: --US model of Moto G7 lacks NFC, international models have it. --The best phone of the G7 line, the Moto G7 Plus, is not offered in the US. This was also the case for the G6 Plus. --US customers are only offered the Moto One of Motorola's Android One line. This model is known as P20 Play in other countries. As with other Moto lines, the "Play" model has the lowest specs. We are not offered the Moto One Vision (this is the one I wanted to buy) or Moto One Power.

Second Moto G Phone and screen craked. I bought this G7 phone after having a G5 phone and getting excellent service from the G5. My purchase was on May 3 and the screen cracked July 12, 2020 weeks after the return date. This phone is not recommended very poor quality and value.
Moto g7. Just what I needed.

The unlocked Motorola Moto G7 is just an amazing phone.. I've had the Moto G7 for a little over 2 weeks now. So far it is an amazing upgrade from the Moto G6. The performance from the G7 is a great upgrade from the G6. But the design is not. The Moto G7 design is just a bigger version of the G6. It also does not have NFC. Not having NFC or a updated design is the only things about the Moto G7 I don't like. I love having 64GB of storage and an SD card slot that allows up to a 128GB card. With the snapdragon 632 processor and 4GB RAM this Moto G7 runs great. Also you can play some games on this phone. On the G7 I can play the Call of Duty Mobile game just fine on medium graphics and high frame rate. The battery is good at 3000MAH.

Wish I didn't own this phone. Blue tooth only works intermittently, Motorola customer service is no help. Volume of alerts is very low, difficult to hear. Without reliable Bluetooth this phone is useless to me. I've owned G4, g6, and now G7. G7 is a junk phone.

It was most perplexing that all my searching found no solution, only more people with the same problem with their Moto G7. I have been a Moto G phone user for years and relied on CNET reviews of the phone which was always their favorite of the budget phones. I owned a Moto G4 initially and loved it so much I upgraded to a Moto G5 when it came out. Right now I am so glad that I kept that Moto G5 because I have put the SIM card back in it and that is my lifeline while I see what will have to be one with my newer G7. The Moto G5 is making calls and working just fine. For anyone interested, I will update this review once I have dealt with Motorola Customer Support.

Moto G7 speaker issue. I owned 5 Moto G phones from G5 and up every year or so. I have always liked the value it provided. however, the G7 and G7 Plus have been disappointing in the build quality. my G7 speaker acting unstable on volume. it goes suddenly small or loud without any change to the phone. the G7 plus Speaker just broke for only 5 month of use. I would stay with Moto for a long time had the quality stayed OK.

The Moto G6 has a 5.7 size screen compared to the Moto G7 6.2, so the bigger the screen, the more battery will be in use. Motorola decided to give the G7 the same 3,000mAh battery capacity as the G6 and relies on the Android Pie's Adaptive Battery feature instead of increasing the Moto G7 battery capacity to atleast 3500mAh. The Moto G7 CPU is more power efficient than the Moto G6, but not enough to offset the smaller battery for it's screen size. Compared to the Moto G7 Play and Power, Motorola decided to remove Band 71 which is a great band for T-Mobile users in rural areas and is going to be a band that T-Mobile is going to use more of. It makes no sense to have Motorola's "lesser" G7 Play and Power to have this band and not the higher spec G7.

While the G7 has a 3000 mAh battery, the G7 Power has a 5000 mAh battery! In my opinion, this one feature makes the G7 Power the only phone in the Motorola "affordable" line of cell phones to get. I returned the G7 to Amazon and so far I am extremely pleased with the G7 Power. Also, there is no reason to purchase the higher storage capcity Moto G7. These phones also accept a micro SD card to expand the storage. I got the G7 Power with only 32 GB of storage then added a 128 GB SD card. Now the only questions are longevity and reliability. We'll see.

The Motorola Moto G7 is not perfect, but it's pretty good... I recommend it.

Solid Phone for Under $300. Compared to unlocked Pixel 3a. G7 good - larger screen, Moto gestures (been using the quick access for flashlight daily for about 5 years now on Moto phones, love it) and value/price. G7 bad - battery doesn't last all day (large screen doesn't help), reception (speeds weren't great and wifi doesn't always switch over to closest AP), 1 speaker has rather low volume, and no wifi calling on Verizon (not Moto's fault as carrier decides which unlocked phones gets all their features so check carrier here as I believe ATT has wifi calling with this same phone). Overall a good phone at the price. I decided to spend the extra $100 and return for a Pixel 3A, which excels in the areas where the G7 is bad. Both are running pure Android, with a few useful extra Moto features/apps on the G7.

Best 'bang for the buck on a budget' phone!. The Motorola Moto G7 has a nice feel and mod design, dual rear cameras and Android 9 Pie. I especially like the turbo charging and excellent battery life. Without a doubt, the Moto G7 is the best value and performance for cost currently available.

RETURNED AFTER 10 DAYS. I bought two of the Moto G7's to use with T-Mobile. I live in Cheyenne, Wyoming where the T-Mobile service is equal to a much bigger city. T-Mobile introduced Band 71 here in Cheyenne back in 2017 as one of two test cities for the country. So I had two main problems with the Moto G7. First of all, the signal was horrendous. I live 6 blocks from the State Capital building and couldn't get much more than 1 bar on the most of the time. If I walked into the basement, zero bars. Go outside in the backyard and Wi-Fi would drop off. Absolutely ridiculous. Yes, there is WI-FI calling so if the bars drop to zero you can still call. But really in a town that has all the T-Mobile bands? It shouldn't happen. So, the antenna used by Motorola is pretty pitiful.

The best of the Moto G7 series (opinion). So far I love everything about the phone. It's fast & responsive. HD screen and all features I would want. Can't really go wrong with a Moto G7 for $59. I had a little trouble configuring this since I wanted to keep my original phone number, since the card that came with it was a Verizon Tracfone card - TF256PSIMV97N - I did a little workaround by getting an AT&T compatible tracfone card - TF123PSIMC4TD and after talking to tech support got my service switched over. The G7 Optimo MAXX is slightly larger than my Moto G6, so naturally I will buy a different case. The touchscreen seems to be more responsive and less sluggish than the previous generation, and call clarity is slightly crisper, though that might be because the old one is due for a cleaning.

My initial opinion is I'm surprised the G7 is available at this price. I think if you decided to purchase the Moto G7 you will be very pleased with what you get out of the box. I know a lot of people are going for the G7 power for the battery life but I will say the regular G7 is definitely worth the purchase as well. Update: I've used this decide for a little over a month now and I still feel like this was a great purchase. I don't get the impression I'm using a mid-range device. Everything about the Moto G7 feels premium. This is my first mid-range phone from Motorola's G series and what Motorola's has done with the G series is a winner in my experience. I decided to format the SD I installed and now it works perfect increasing the storage capacity in my phone.

I really wanted this phone to work for me. This is now my fourth g series phone in two months (g6 plus international, g6, and two g7's). I guess you can't say I give up easily. After going rounds with Moto tech support and returning three phones to Amazon (fourth phone will be returned shortly) I'm done with the g series for now. I wanted these phones to work for me. Coming off of two prior great Moto experiences (last one being Moto x pure edition - the battery caved) I was ready to go to a new model. But, neither the g6 nor g7 will be that model. To be clear, I really like these phones. Style is great. Size is wonderful. Battery life is outstanding. Bloatware is minimal. Cameras are crisp. They are fast and responsive phones. Good stuff! But, what should be the primary function of a phone?

I was thoroughly disappointed - not only comparing the G7 to the Asus but even to the previous Moto G phones. Storage says it's only 21% full but "Storage space is running out. Some system functions may not work.". Motorola's second level tech support says the software isn't working. Apparently the mods Amazon made to force their software from being removed broke the file management for the Moto G7 sad
The Right Phone. The Moto G7 phone is the right phone. Simple to use and good battery life. Easy to set up with Mint Mobile.

Poor man's Samsung S10 - Works nearly as well at less than half the price. User experience comparable to my work Samsung S10. While the Samsung's screen is better, the nifty fingerprint sensor works only with an expensive, difficult to install, screen protector. Since the Samsung screen sticks out from the body, a screen protector is a must. Point to Moto G7 for useful fingerprint sensor. Point to Samsung for somewhat nicer screen. Samsung S10 also comes with 128 GB of memory while Moto G7 came with 64, plus expansion slot. NOTE: Moto G7 expansion slot works ONLY with SDXC 2 or UHS-II memory card. A compatible 64 GB card cost me just over $60 on Amazon. If not for the cost of the card, I would have said the Moto G7 is A THIRD the price of the Samsung. I'm not enough of a camera geek to compare cameras.

Be aware of the meaning of International and Global. The Moto G7, is for the most part a very good cell phone. However, I was misled by the discription of Global Unlocked, International. What I found this to be, after some time on the phone with Motorola Rep. was: it was made in Bolgaria! So all the downloads take forever! And several apps are not accessible. This is why I after speaking with Motorola... I decided to return this phone.

In general, the G7+ is the first Motorola phone that I have been motivated to try since using the Moto X Pure/Style of 2015, one of my old favorites. The G7+ is much faster, has a better camera, newer software (Android 9 with January 2019 security), and has comparable speakers.

Performs well yet not expensive. This phone is not pricey but works very well. Long battery life. Snappy performance. I bought two of these phones. I purchased my second Moto g7 after the first (very sadly) met an early death after being dropped from quite a height. Very sad. It had been a great phone and did not deserve that date. But You liked it so much I bought another Moto g7. And hopefully will treat this one much better. The G7 is not pricey but performs really well. Good connectivity. Responsive screen. Good GPS.
Best Android for the money. I'm a Moto fan. They are the best budget phones. I lost a G5+ due to battery failure, but my G7 is still the best. I'm very happy with it.

Love My New Phone. I am a very happy customer with this phone. I sent back the first unlocked phone I tried (different brand) because I couldn't get it to work on my network. I purchased this one because it said it came with 30 days support from Amazon and it had the features I was looking for. I did not need the support even once. I use T-mobile full service (not pay as you go). Here's how I set up the phone. Put your SIM card in and then when you power up, plug it in to charge it up and leave it charging for the next few steps. Follow the instructions to connect to your wi-fi network. I have learned this is a critical step. I took my first phone to T-Mobile who really didn't understand that step.

Used, no mobile data, but fixed with reset.. It's too son to give a full review. Bought the phone through Amazon Warehouse, used. Out of the box, once new SIM was installed, it was unable to connect for mobile data. after a few hours horsing around with settings, I called Amazon support who connected me with Motorola support and was instructed how to reset Wifi, data and Bluetooth... voila. A small fix like this can be very frustrating and probably causes a large number of returns. Knowledgeable support staff makes the difference, so kudos to Amazon (Brian) and Motorola (Princess). I like the functionality and ease of use of the phone, so far is very good. The lack of carrier bloat ware is nice. Outside of this hiccup, I have a better opinion of reburbished (but that wasn't explicit in the description) phones and buying through Amazon.
